Code Title 27, Chapter 36A) plus the NAIC Valuation Manual edition operative for the 12/31 valuation date (VM-20 life PBR, VM-21 variable annuity, VM-25 health, VM-A/VM-C prescribed tables), re-read each January against the NAIC-published operative Valuation Manual; Arizona, California and Connecticut Standard Valuation Laws confirmed to adopt the same operative edition

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and 12/31 statutory reserve computation for every in-force policy and contract of the Accident and health, life and annuity blocks, from policy admin extract through exclusion testing, deterministic and stochastic runs, aggregation to the VM-20 Section 2 minimum reserve and posting to Exhibits 5 and 6

In-scope systems.value: Valuation models and prescribed table libraries in the actuarial modeling platform, fed by the seriatim in-force extract from the policy administration system and reconciled to the general ledger

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Reserve Valuation Procedure - valuation date lock, extract and data-quality gate, exclusion tests, assumption set approval, NPR/DR/SR runs, reinsurance credit, aggregation, roll-forward attribution and GL posting, with a per-product mapping to the prescribed standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary under the VM-G governance framework, re-approved annually before the Q4 valuation and on any NAIC Valuation Manual amendment effective 1 January

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly reserve close by working day 8 after 3/31, 6/30 and 9/30 to support the 5/15, 8/15 and 11/15 quarterly statements; annual reserve lock by working day 15 of January so the 12/31 figure supports the 1 March Annual Statement to the Alabama Department of Insurance

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar tasks at extract-ready, assumption-freeze, model-lock and reserve-sign-off milestones, with alerts to the Valuation Actuary and Appointed Actuary 5 and 2 working days before each milestone

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Reserve computation exceptions - failed exclusion test not re-run, unapproved assumption, out-of-tolerance data reconciliation, post-lock model change - logged with the affected Annual Statement line, dollar impact and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every reserve restatement, post-lock model change and unresolved exclusion-test failure before the figure is released to Statutory Reporting

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Seriatim extract to policy admin control totals within 0.1 percent on count and face amount and 0.5 percent on reserve dollars; any segment where the reported reserve is below the recomputed minimum reserve is a fail regardless of size; more than two segment fails escalates to the Chief Actuary and the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs quarterly with a full annual certification, so the test runs quarterly at reduced scope on the largest five segments and in full at 12/31 across all segments

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, calibrated or run any sampled valuation model in the period under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly reserve computation test workpaper - population extract, segment sample, independent re-performance runs, tolerance calculations and exception log - filed in the model governance repository under the valuation date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Reserve summary by Annual Statement line tied to Exhibits 5 and 6, exclusion test results, assumption memo and model run logs, presentable to an ALDOI financial examiner within 10 business days of an information request

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers valuation-methodology questions from the Alabama Department of Insurance and any lead state examiner; the Statutory Reporting Manager routes the request and Regulatory Counsel clears anything touching a restatement before it is sent

checklist.step: Lock the valuation date and map every product to its prescribed standard
actions: Open the valuation scope register and list every product code in force at the valuation date, taking the product list from the Insurance Product Manager and the writing-company mapping from the Statutory Reporting Manager.

Against each product code record the governing standard: VM-20 for post-2020 issue life, pre-Valuation-Manual CRVM for grandfathered life, VM-21 for variable annuity and guaranteed benefit contracts, VM-25 for accident and health contract and claim reserves, VM-22 for non-variable annuity.
Record for each product the issue-year cohort, the Annual Statement line and the Exhibit 5 or Exhibit 6 row it lands on.
Flag every product where the standard changed at 1 January because of a Valuation Manual amendment and note the amendment reference on the row.
Circulate the locked scope register to the Appointed Actuary and Chief Actuary and freeze it - later additions require a written scope change.
checklist.done: every in-force product code carries a named prescribed standard, issue-year cohort and Annual Statement line on a frozen scope register.

checklist.step: Pull the seriatim in-force extract as of the valuation date
actions: Run the valuation extract job against the policy administration system with the as-of date set to the last calendar day of the valuation quarter and the cut-off set after the month-end nightly cycle has completed.

Include per policy: policy number, plan code, issue date, issue age, sex, smoker class, underwriting class, face amount, account value, gross and net premium, paid-to date, mode, rider codes, reinsurance treaty codes and status.
Produce control totals - policy count, total face amount, total account value and annualized premium - by plan code and hand them to the Valuation Actuary in the same file as the data.
Load the extract to the valuation staging area in the enterprise data warehouse with the run id, job timestamp and source system release number stamped on every row.
Notify the Actuarial Analyst that the extract is ready and lock the staging table against further writes.
checklist.done: a dated, locked seriatim extract with per-plan-code control totals and a stamped run id is available in the valuation staging area.

checklist.step: Clear the data-quality gate before any model is run
actions: Run the valuation data-quality rule set over the staging table: null issue date, issue age outside 0-99, missing sex or smoker class, negative account value, face amount of zero on an in-force life policy, paid-to date more than 90 days before the valuation date.
Compare the extract control totals to the policy administration in-force report and to the prior quarter, and explain any movement over 2 percent by plan code.
Route every failing record to the Policy Administration Analyst for correction at source, and record the count of records defaulted rather than corrected.
Write the VM-31 data section input - record counts, failure counts, defaults applied and their justification - into the data quality summary.
Sign the gate open only when defaulted records are under the agreed 0.5 percent of reserve dollars, otherwise escalate to the Valuation Actuary.
checklist.done: the data quality summary shows every rule result, defaults are within tolerance and the gate is signed open with a named signer and date.

checklist.step: Refresh and get approval for the valuation assumption set
actions: Pull the company experience studies for mortality, lapse, premium persistency, partial withdrawal and, for health, claim termination and trend, and state the credibility method and exposure period used.
Blend company experience to the prescribed industry basis using the VM-20 Section 9 credibility procedure and record the resulting margin for each assumption.
Document every prudent estimate assumption with its anticipated experience, its margin and the rationale, in the format VM-31 requires.
Table the assumption set to the actuarial governance forum for approval and record the approval date, attendees and any conditions.
Load the approved assumptions into the actuarial modeling platform assumption library under a new version tag and freeze the version.
checklist.done: every prudent estimate assumption is documented with anticipated experience, margin and rationale, approved and frozen under a version tag.

checklist.step: Load the prescribed tables and set the maximum valuation interest rate
actions: Load the prescribed mortality tables from VM-M for the issue-year cohorts in scope - 2017 CSO for the net premium reserve, VBT-based industry tables for the deterministic and stochastic reserves.
Look up the calendar-year maximum valuation interest rate from the NAIC-published rates for each product type and guarantee duration and enter it against each cohort.
Enter the prescribed valuation method by cohort - net level, CRVM, or the VM-20 net premium reserve - and the reserve floor applicable to each.
Reconcile the loaded table identifiers and rates line by line to the source NAIC publication with a second reviewer initialling each row.
Save the table set under the same version tag as the assumption set so runs are reproducible.
checklist.done: prescribed tables, valuation interest rates and valuation methods are loaded, dual-checked against the NAIC source and version tagged.

checklist.step: Run the VM-20 exclusion tests for each life reserving group
actions: For each VM-20 reserving group run the Stochastic Exclusion Ratio Test and record the numerator, denominator and resulting ratio against the 6 percent threshold.
Where the group qualifies, run the Deterministic Exclusion Test comparing the net premium reserve to the deterministic reserve and record the result.
For any group that fails a test, remove the exclusion and schedule the full stochastic or deterministic run in the same cycle - never carry a failed exclusion forward.
Save the test output pack with the scenario set identifier and hand a copy to the Appointed Actuary, who must certify the exclusion in the VM-31 report.
Record on the scope register which reserve components each group must therefore compute.
checklist.done: every reserving group has a dated exclusion test result with its ratio, and every failing group is scheduled for the full run.

checklist.step: Compute the net premium reserve and the formulaic reserves
actions: Run the net premium reserve model seriatim for the VM-20 blocks using the loaded prescribed tables and the calendar-year maximum valuation interest rate.
Run the CRVM and net level reserves for the grandfathered pre-Valuation-Manual cohorts on their original issue-year basis.
Apply the deficiency reserve test where gross premiums are below the valuation net premium and post any deficiency reserve arising.
Extract reserves per policy and aggregate to plan code, then to Annual Statement line, and store the seriatim output for audit trail.
Compare the seriatim result to the prior quarter on a like-for-like in-force basis and investigate any plan code moving more than 3 percent per unit of face amount.
checklist.done: net premium and formulaic reserves are computed seriatim, aggregated to Annual Statement line, and per-unit movements over 3 percent are explained.

checklist.step: Run the deterministic reserve on the prescribed single scenario
actions: Set the starting asset portfolio for each model segment to the amount required to reproduce the segment cash flows, taking the asset file from the Investment Operations Manager as of the valuation date.
Run the gross premium valuation on the prescribed deterministic scenario using the approved prudent estimate assumptions and the prescribed discount rates.
Record the present value of benefits and expenses less the present value of premiums, and the resulting deterministic reserve by reserving group.
Check the reinvestment and disinvestment assumptions used match the VM-20 prescribed spreads and default costs, and log the assumed asset mix.
Save the run log with the model version, assumption version tag, scenario id and machine run time.
checklist.done: a deterministic reserve exists per reserving group with a saved run log naming model version, assumption version and scenario id.

checklist.step: Run the stochastic reserve and take the CTE 70 measure
actions: Generate or load the prescribed economic scenario set for the valuation date and confirm the scenario count and the calibration criteria are met.
Run the full stochastic projection for every group that failed the stochastic exclusion test, projecting the greatest present value of accumulated deficiency for each scenario.
Rank the scenario results and compute CTE 70 as the average of the worst 30 percent, then add the prescribed additional amounts.
Where a scenario reduction technique is used, document the method, the number of scenarios retained and the validation that the reduced set reproduces the full-set CTE within tolerance.
Hand the stochastic reserve by reserving group to the Valuation Actuary with the scenario file identifier attached.
checklist.done: a documented CTE 70 stochastic reserve exists per required reserving group with the scenario set identified and any scenario reduction validated.

checklist.step: Compute the accident and health reserves under VM-25
actions: Compute the unearned premium reserve on the gross modal premium in force at the valuation date, split by policy form.

Compute claim reserves for open and incurred-but-not-reported accident and health claims using the prescribed morbidity and claim termination tables, taking the claim inventory from the Claims Director / Manager.
Compute contract reserves for the level-premium and non-cancellable forms using the prescribed valuation net premium method and interest rate.
Run the premium deficiency reserve test by grouping of contracts and post a deficiency reserve where projected claims plus expenses exceed projected premiums plus existing reserves.
Reconcile the resulting reserves to the Annual Statement Exhibit 6 rows and to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit claim development.
checklist.done: unearned premium, claim, contract and any premium deficiency reserves are computed by policy form and tie to Exhibit 6.

checklist.step: Compute the ceded reinsurance reserve credit and the direct-to-net bridge
actions: Pull the treaty inventory and per-policy cession detail from the reinsurance administration system as of the valuation date and match it to the seriatim in-force extract on policy number and treaty code.
Compute the ceded reserve on the same valuation basis as the direct reserve and apply the VM-20 Section 8 reinsurance requirements including any cash-flow-based credit limits.

Confirm each assuming reinsurer is authorised, certified or has qualifying collateral, taking the current status from the Reinsurance Credit and Security Analyst, and restrict the credit where it is not.
Produce the direct less ceded equals net bridge by Annual Statement line and tie it to Schedule S Part 3.
List every unmatched cession and every policy with a treaty code that has no reserve credit and clear them before lock.
checklist.done: a direct-ceded-net reserve bridge ties to Schedule S Part 3 with no unmatched cessions and reinsurer status verified for every credit taken.

checklist.step: Aggregate to the minimum reserve and prove the floors hold
actions: For each VM-20 reserving group take the minimum reserve as the greater of the net premium reserve and the applicable deterministic or stochastic reserve, less the due and deferred premium asset, per VM-20 Section 2.
Confirm no segment reports a reserve below its statutory floor - cash surrender value for life, unearned premium for health - and list any that would.
Aggregate to Annual Statement line and writing company, then to the Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 6 presentation rows.
Compute the aggregate reserve for the Alabama-domiciled writing company separately so the ALDOI filing figure is directly traceable.
Route the aggregation worksheet to the Appointed Actuary for the reserve adequacy view before lock.
checklist.done: the minimum reserve by group is the documented greater-of result, no floor is breached, and totals tie to Exhibits 5 and 6.

checklist.step: Clear model change control and validation before the figure is released
actions: List every model change made since the prior valuation from the model change log, with the requester, the reason and the code or configuration diff.
Require a quantified before-and-after reserve impact for each change and refuse to sign any change with no impact run.
Confirm each change has a completed independent validation note and that the model version deployed matches the version validated.
Check the run logs show the frozen assumption version tag and the correct scenario set were used - a run on a stale tag must be re-run.
Record the sign-off in the model governance repository against the valuation date.
checklist.done: every model change since the prior valuation carries a quantified impact, a validation note and a dated sign-off in the model governance repository.

checklist.step: Produce the reserve roll-forward and attribution of change
actions: Build the roll-forward from the prior valuation reserve to the current one with the standard steps: new business, in-force movement and decrements, interest accretion, assumption change, method or model change, reinsurance change, and true-up.
Quantify each step by Annual Statement line and require the steps to sum to the actual movement within 0.5 percent before the roll-forward is accepted.
Write a one-paragraph explanation for any step over 2 percent of the opening reserve and name the driver, not the mechanism.
Circulate the roll-forward to the Chief Financial Officer and the Statutory Reporting Manager as the reserve movement narrative for the quarter.
Attach the roll-forward to the valuation workpaper pack.
checklist.done: a signed roll-forward reconciles opening to closing reserves within 0.5 percent with every material step explained by driver.

checklist.step: Post the reserves to the ledger and archive the valuation workpapers
actions: Post the reserve journal by writing company and Annual Statement line, referencing the valuation run id in the journal narrative.
Tie the posted balances to the aggregation worksheet and to Exhibit 5, Exhibit 6 and Page 3 of the Annual Statement, and clear any difference before close.

Assemble the valuation workpaper pack - scope register, extract control totals, data quality summary, assumption memo, exclusion tests, run logs, aggregation worksheet, reinsurance bridge, roll-forward.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository indexed by valuation date, writing company and Annual Statement line with a 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository entry is retrievable by valuation date and reserving group before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: reserves are posted and tied to Exhibits 5 and 6, and the full workpaper pack is archived under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve segments reported for the valuation date
actions: Extract every reserve line reported in Exhibit 5, Exhibit 6 and the Analysis of Increase in Reserves for the valuation date from the statutory reporting workbook, by writing company.
Add every reserving group listed on the valuation scope register so a segment cannot be omitted from the statement and escape the test.
Reconcile the extracted total to the reserve balance in the general ledger and to Page 3 of the Annual Statement, and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete, naming the extract date and the report versions used.
testing.done: the population reconciles to Page 3 and the general ledger and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the seriatim extract back to the policy administration source of record
actions: Re-run the in-force count, face amount, account value and annualized premium totals directly from the policy administration system for the valuation date.
Compare each total to the control totals recorded on the valuation extract and compute the variance by plan code.
Treat any plan code outside 0.1 percent on count or face amount, or 0.5 percent on reserve dollars, as an exception whatever the explanation offered.
Confirm the data quality gate was signed before the first model run by comparing the gate signature timestamp to the earliest run log timestamp.
testing.done: every plan code is within tolerance to the policy administration source, and the gate signature pre-dates the first model run.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of reserving groups and policies
actions: Take 100 percent of reserving groups holding more than 5 percent of total reserves and 100 percent of groups that failed an exclusion test.
Take 10 further groups at random using a recorded seed, and within each sampled group draw 25 seriatim policies at random.
Record the seed, population size, stratification boundaries and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every segment with a prior-period exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all large and exclusion-failing groups plus prior exceptions is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the prescribed-standard mapping for each sampled group
actions: For each sampled group read the product specification and issue-year cohort and reach an independent conclusion on the governing standard before looking at the scope register.
Check the conclusion against the operative NAIC Valuation Manual edition for the valuation date, not a later or earlier edition.
Compare to the recorded mapping; a right standard cited to the wrong Valuation Manual section is still an exception.
Capture the Valuation Manual section relied on into the workpaper for each sampled group.
testing.done: each sampled group has an independent standard determination with the operative Valuation Manual section captured.

testing.step: Independently recompute the net premium reserve on the sampled policies
actions: Build a standalone recomputation for each of the 25 sampled policies per group using the 2017 CSO table, the issue-year maximum valuation interest rate and the prescribed valuation method.
Source the policy attributes - issue date, issue age, sex, smoker class, face amount, paid-to date - from the policy administration record, not from the valuation extract.
Compare the recomputed reserve to the model output per policy and flag any policy differing by more than 1 percent or 500 dollars, whichever is greater.
Trace each flagged difference to a cause - wrong table, wrong interest rate, wrong method, wrong policy attribute - and record it.
testing.done: every sampled policy is recomputed from source attributes and every difference over tolerance has a named cause.

testing.step: Verify the prescribed tables and valuation interest rates loaded in the model
actions: Open the assumption and table library for the frozen version tag and export the loaded mortality table identifiers and valuation interest rates by cohort.
Compare each identifier and rate to the NAIC-published prescribed tables and calendar-year rates for the valuation date, row by row.
Confirm the version tag stamped on each production run log matches the frozen tag, and list any run made on an unfrozen or superseded tag.
Screenshot the library version detail and the NAIC source page into the workpaper.
testing.done: loaded tables and rates agree line by line with the NAIC source and every production run used the frozen version tag.

testing.step: Re-perform the exclusion test arithmetic and the greater-of aggregation
actions: For each sampled group recompute the stochastic exclusion ratio from the model output numerator and denominator and compare it to the 6 percent threshold.
Confirm every group failing the test actually has a stochastic reserve run in the cycle and that the CTE 70 figure was carried into aggregation.
Recompute the minimum reserve as the greater of the net premium reserve and the applicable deterministic or stochastic reserve, less the due and deferred premium asset.
Compare to the reported reserve; any segment reported below the recomputed minimum is a fail regardless of dollar size.
testing.done: exclusion ratios and greater-of aggregation are recomputed and no sampled segment is reported below its recomputed minimum.

testing.step: Test the ceded reinsurance credit and its Schedule S trace
actions: Select the ten largest ceded reserve credits and open each treaty in the reinsurance administration system to confirm the cession is in force at the valuation date.
Confirm the ceded reserve is computed on the same valuation basis as the direct reserve and that any VM-20 Section 8 limitation was applied.
Check each assuming reinsurer status - authorised, certified or collateralised - against the current schedule and recompute the allowed credit where the reinsurer is unauthorised.
Trace the direct-ceded-net bridge to Schedule S Part 3 and to the reserve journal in the general ledger.
testing.done: each sampled credit ties to an in-force treaty, a verified reinsurer status and Schedule S Part 3.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the reserving group, the Annual Statement line, the dollar impact and whether the reported reserve was understated.
Assign a root cause - extract defect, stale assumption tag, unvalidated model change, wrong prescribed table, exclusion test not re-run - and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next valuation cycle and, for any understatement, refer the item to the Appointed Actuary for a materiality assessment against the opinion.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the reserve computation test
actions: Compute the exception rate by count and by reserve dollars and compare it to the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the Model Risk Manager, who built and ran none of the sampled models, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any reserve understatement to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Code Title 27, Chapter 36A) and the Academy of Actuaries US Qualification Standards for the statement of actuarial opinion; Arizona, California and Connecticut confirmed to require the same VM-30 opinion form

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Audit Committee, which also makes the annual Appointed Actuary appointment resolution and receives the opinion outcome; reviewed each October ahead of the year-end cycle

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Opinion signed and dated no later than the Annual Statement filing date of 1 March; Actuarial Memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary available to the Alabama Department of Insurance by 15 March; VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report available by 1 April

Deadline reminders configured.value: Year-end calendar tasks at 15 October appointment confirmation, 15 January scope and reliance lock, 10 February peer review complete, 25 February signature, 15 March memorandum, 1 April VM-31 report, each alerting the Appointed Actuary and Chief Actuary

checklist.step: Confirm the board appointment of the Appointed Actuary is current
actions: Pull the board or Audit Committee resolution appointing the Appointed Actuary and confirm it names the individual, the writing companies covered and the effective date.
Confirm the appointment is on file with the Alabama Department of Insurance and with each other state that requires notification of the appointment or of a change.
Where the appointed individual has changed in the year, confirm the notification of change was sent to the domiciliary commissioner within the required window and file the acknowledgement.
Publish the current appointment record to the Chief Actuary and file it in the board portal against the year-end cycle.
checklist.done: a current board resolution names the Appointed Actuary and the covered writing companies, and the domiciliary regulator holds the appointment on file.

checklist.step: Evidence that the signer meets the Qualification Standards
actions: Confirm the signer holds the required membership and designation and meets the specific qualification requirements for the statement of actuarial opinion.

Collect the signer's continuing education record for the year - hours by subject, including the professionalism and the relevant-topic requirements - and check it against the US Qualification Standards.
Where experience rather than education supports a subject area, record the specific engagements relied on.
File the qualification attestation, signed and dated by the individual, with the opinion workpapers.
checklist.done: a dated qualification attestation with a supporting continuing education record is on file for the signing individual.

checklist.step: Fix the scope of the opinion and the reserve items covered
actions: List every reserve and related actuarial item to be covered - Exhibit 5 aggregate reserves for life and annuity, Exhibit 6 accident and health reserves, Exhibit 7 deposit-type contracts, claim reserves and any additional actuarial liabilities.
Take the reported amounts from the Statutory Reporting Manager as they will appear in the Annual Statement, not from a draft valuation summary.
Identify any item deliberately excluded from the opinion and state the reason on the scope worksheet.
Agree the scope in writing with the Chief Financial Officer so the opinion and the statement cannot diverge.
Freeze the scope worksheet by 15 January and log any later change as an exception.
checklist.done: a frozen scope worksheet lists every covered reserve item with its Annual Statement amount and names any exclusion with its reason.

checklist.step: Obtain the reliance letters for data and for work performed by others
actions: Request a signed reliance letter from the officer responsible for the in-force, claim and asset data, stating the data was prepared for this purpose and is accurate and complete.
Request reliance letters from any other actuary whose work is relied on - the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary for cash-flow testing, the Reinsurance Actuary for ceded credits, any external consultant.
Check each letter names the specific data or work relied on, the valuation date and the signer's role, and reject generic letters.
List the reliances that will be named in the opinion body and match the list to the letters held.
File all letters in the opinion folder before drafting the reliance paragraphs.
checklist.done: every reliance named in the opinion is backed by a specific, signed and dated reliance letter in the opinion folder.

checklist.step: Draft the opinion to the VM-30 prescribed wording
actions: Open the VM-30 Section 3 prescribed opinion form for the operative year and draft the identification, scope, reliance and opinion sections in the prescribed order.

Insert the standard opinion paragraphs stating the reserves are computed in accordance with accepted actuarial standards and meet the requirements of the laws of Alabama, and are at least as great as the minimum required by the Standard Valuation Law.
Complete Exhibit A of the opinion with the reserve amounts by category and Exhibit B with the key indicators the form requires.
Do not paraphrase - where the form prescribes wording, use it verbatim and confine company-specific text to the scope and reliance sections.
Version the draft in the document management repository so every wording change is traceable to a reviewer comment.
checklist.done: a draft opinion follows the VM-30 prescribed form section by section with Exhibits A and B populated from the frozen scope worksheet.

checklist.step: Reach and document the asset adequacy conclusion
actions: Take the asset adequacy testing results from the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary, including the scenario results and any additional reserve indicated.
Decide whether the reserves make good and sufficient provision for the anticipated cash flows and record the basis for that judgement.
Where additional reserves are needed, agree the amount with the Chief Financial Officer and confirm it is booked before the statement is filed.
Where the conclusion is qualified in any way, draft the qualification language explicitly rather than softening the standard paragraph.
Record the conclusion, the amount of any additional reserve and the date on the opinion workpaper.
checklist.done: the asset adequacy conclusion is stated with its basis, and any additional reserve indicated is booked before filing.

checklist.step: Draft the Actuarial Memorandum sections required by VM-30
actions: Write the memorandum sections VM-30 requires: description of the business covered, reserve methods and bases, asset adequacy methodology, assumptions with their sources, model description and validation, and the summary of results.
Describe every material assumption with its anticipated experience, margin and rationale so a reviewing actuary could reproduce the result.
Include the sensitivity results and state which assumptions the conclusion is most exposed to.
Cross-reference each section to the underlying valuation workpaper so the memorandum is navigable during an examination.
Hand the draft to the Appointed Actuary at least two weeks before the 15 March availability date.
checklist.done: a complete memorandum covering every VM-30 required section is drafted and cross-referenced to the valuation workpapers.

checklist.step: Prepare the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary
actions: Prepare the summary VM-30 requires for the domiciliary commissioner, covering the material changes in assumptions or methods from the prior year and the reasons for them.
State the extent to which the reserves are adequate under moderately adverse conditions and describe any block where they are not.
Describe any reserve strengthening or release recorded in the year and its driver.
Confirm the summary is dated no later than 15 March and marked for the domiciliary commissioner's use.
checklist.done: a dated Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary covering assumption changes, adequacy and reserve movements is ready by 15 March.

checklist.step: Assemble the VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report for the principle-based blocks
actions: Assemble the VM-31 report sections for every VM-20 and VM-21 block: overview, reserving group definitions, assumptions and margins, model description, exclusion test results, cash flow model description and the certifications VM-31 requires.
Include the data section describing record counts, data quality checks, defaults applied and their justification, taken from the data quality summary.
Obtain the certifications VM-31 names - the qualified actuary certification on assumptions and margins and the certification on model inputs from the responsible officer.
Target completion by 1 April and log any section not complete by that date as an exception.
checklist.done: a complete VM-31 report with all required sections and certifications is available by 1 April.

checklist.step: Put the opinion and memorandum through independent peer review
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary who did not prepare the reserves or the asset adequacy testing.
The reviewer checks the opinion wording against the VM-30 prescribed form clause by clause and the Exhibit A amounts against the statutory reporting workbook.
The reviewer challenges each material assumption and margin against the experience study and records the challenge and the response.
Every review comment is dispositioned in writing - accepted with a change, or rejected with a reason - before signature.
File the review record with the opinion workpapers, naming the reviewer and the review date.
checklist.done: a named independent reviewer has signed a review record with every comment dispositioned before signature.

checklist.step: Tie the opinion exhibits to the filed Annual Statement figures
actions: Compare every amount in Exhibit A of the opinion to the corresponding Exhibit 5, Exhibit 6 and Exhibit 7 line in the statement being filed, cell by cell.
Confirm the writing company name, NAIC company code and statement year on the opinion match the statement cover page.
Where a late statement adjustment changes a reserve, re-issue Exhibit A rather than filing an opinion that disagrees with the statement.
Sign the tie-out sheet and attach it to the opinion folder.
checklist.done: a signed tie-out sheet shows every Exhibit A amount agreeing to the statement being filed, with company code and year matching.

checklist.step: Sign and date the opinion
actions: Sign the opinion personally in the signature block, adding the designation, address and the date of signature.
Date the opinion no later than the 1 March Annual Statement filing date and never earlier than the date the tie-out and peer review completed.
Produce the signed PDF, apply the file naming convention of company code, statement year and document type, and lock it against further edit.
Hand the locked PDF to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for filing and keep the executed original in the opinion folder.
checklist.done: a signed, dated and locked opinion PDF exists, dated on or before 1 March and after peer review completion.

checklist.step: Report the opinion outcome to the Board Audit Committee
actions: Present to the Audit Committee the opinion type issued, the asset adequacy conclusion, any additional reserve booked and any qualification.
Present the material assumption changes from the prior year and their reserve impact, taken from the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary.
Record the committee's acknowledgement in the minutes and note any action the committee directs.
File the presentation and minute extract in the board portal against the opinion year.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee minutes record the opinion type, adequacy conclusion and any qualification for the year.

checklist.step: Log any qualification or late section as a compliance exception
actions: Raise an issue for any opinion that is qualified, adverse or inconclusive, naming the block and the reason.
Raise an issue for any memorandum section not complete by 15 March or VM-31 section not complete by 1 April, with the days late recorded.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Board Audit Committee.
Track the issue to closure and confirm the remediation is reflected in the following year's cycle plan.
checklist.done: every qualification and every late section is an open issue with an owner, days late and a remediation date.

checklist.step: Archive the opinion package for the retention period
actions: Move the signed opinion, memorandum, Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary, VM-31 report, reliance letters, peer review record, qualification attestation and board resolution into the compliance evidence repository.
Index the package by writing company, NAIC company code and statement year and apply the 7-year retention label.
Mark the memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary as confidential under the Standard Valuation Law confidentiality provisions and restrict access accordingly.
Confirm the package is retrievable by company code and statement year before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the full opinion package is archived, confidentiality-marked, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by company code and year.

testing.step: Build the population of opinions and supporting documents for the year
actions: List every writing company required to file a Statement of Actuarial Opinion for the statement year from the entity register held by the Statutory Reporting Manager.
For each, locate the signed opinion, memorandum, Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary and VM-31 report in the evidence repository.
Reconcile the count of opinions to the count of Annual Statements filed and investigate any company with a statement but no opinion.
Sign the population as complete, naming the entity register version used.
testing.done: the opinion population reconciles one-to-one to the filed Annual Statements and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Verify the appointment and qualification of every signer
actions: Open the board or Audit Committee resolution for each writing company and confirm it names the individual who actually signed and covers the statement year.
Confirm the appointment, and any change of appointed individual, was notified to the domiciliary commissioner and that the acknowledgement is on file.
Read the signer's continuing education record and test the hours by subject against the US Qualification Standards requirement for the statement of actuarial opinion.
Treat a signature by an individual without a current appointment or with a shortfall in the specific qualification requirements as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every signature traces to a current board appointment and a qualification record that meets the standard.

testing.step: Draw the sample of opinion sections and reliances to re-perform
actions: Take 100 percent of opinions for companies with reserves above the materiality threshold and 100 percent of any qualified opinion.
For each sampled opinion take every named reliance and 10 Exhibit A lines selected at random with a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every prior-year exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all material and qualified opinions, their reliances and selected exhibit lines is documented.

testing.step: Compare the opinion wording clause by clause to the VM-30 prescribed form
actions: Open the VM-30 Section 3 prescribed opinion form for the operative year and lay it beside each sampled signed opinion.
Compare the identification, scope, reliance and opinion paragraphs clause by clause and mark every omission, addition or reworded prescribed sentence.
Confirm the opinion states the reserves meet the requirements of the laws of Alabama and are at least as great as the minimum required by the Standard Valuation Law.
Treat any reworded prescribed paragraph as a fail even where the meaning appears preserved.
testing.done: each sampled opinion matches the prescribed form clause by clause or the deviation is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Trace Exhibit A amounts to the filed Annual Statement
actions: Open the filed Annual Statement for each sampled company and locate Exhibits 5, 6 and 7 as filed, not as drafted.
Compare each sampled Exhibit A line to the corresponding statement line and record any difference to the dollar.
Confirm the company name, NAIC company code and statement year on the opinion match the statement cover page.
Capture the statement page and the opinion exhibit page into the workpaper side by side.
testing.done: every sampled Exhibit A line agrees to the filed statement to the dollar, with both pages captured.

testing.step: Test every named reliance against a signed reliance letter
actions: Pull the reliance letter behind each named reliance and confirm it is signed, dated and names the specific data or work relied on and the valuation date.
Confirm the letter pre-dates the opinion signature date - a letter dated after signature does not support the opinion.
Confirm the person signing the data reliance letter is the officer responsible for the data, not a delegate without that responsibility.
Record any reliance named in the opinion with no matching letter as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every named reliance has a specific, signed letter dated before the opinion signature or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the date and deadline arithmetic on the package
actions: Compare the opinion signature date to the Annual Statement filing date and confirm it is on or before 1 March.
Confirm the signature date is on or after the peer review completion date and the tie-out sheet date.
Compare the memorandum completion date to 15 March and the VM-31 report completion date to 1 April and compute days late where either is missed.
Confirm the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary is dated no later than 15 March and addressed to the domiciliary commissioner.
testing.done: every date in the package is recomputed against its deadline and any lateness is quantified in days.

testing.step: Challenge the asset adequacy conclusion and any qualification
actions: Read the asset adequacy results underlying each sampled opinion and reach an independent view on whether the reserves make good and sufficient provision.
Where an additional reserve was indicated, trace the booked amount to the general ledger and to Exhibit 5 or 6 in the filed statement.
Where the opinion is unqualified but the testing shows a shortfall in any block, escalate immediately rather than logging it as a routine exception.
Record the independent view and the evidence relied on in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent adequacy view is recorded for each sampled opinion and any indicated additional reserve is traced to the filed statement.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the writing company, the opinion section or document affected and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause - lapsed appointment, qualification shortfall, missing reliance letter, wording deviation, late memorandum, exhibit disagreement - and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current cycle where the opinion can still be corrected, and notify the Board Audit Committee where it cannot.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the opinion test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for appointment, qualification, prescribed wording and memorandum timeliness.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references for each supporting finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither drafted nor peer reviewed any sampled opinion, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion to the Board Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Code Title 27, Chapter 36A and Section 27-3-26) requiring the opinion to accompany the Annual Statement, read with the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions filing checklist for the statement year; Arizona, California and Connecticut filing checklists confirmed for their own copy and hard-copy requirements

checklist.step: Build the jurisdiction matrix from the current licence register
actions: Export the certificate of authority register and list every state and territory in which each writing company is licensed at 31 December, giving the full 51-jurisdiction scope.
Add for each row the NAIC company code, the state department name, and whether the state accepts the NAIC Financial Data Repository copy or requires its own submission.
Mark the states that require a hard-copy or wet-signature opinion and the states with a filing fee attached to the annual statement.
Reconcile the matrix row count to the prior year and investigate any licence added or surrendered in the year with the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Freeze the matrix on 15 January as the filing target list.
checklist.done: a frozen matrix lists every writing-company and jurisdiction pair with its submission channel, hard-copy flag and fee.

checklist.step: Pull the current-year filing checklist for each state
actions: Open the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for the statement year and extract the filing checklist covering the actuarial opinion, memorandum and supplemental filings.
For each state on the matrix, open the department's annual statement filing checklist or bulletin for the year and record any requirement that differs from the NAIC baseline.
Record per state the due date, the accepted format, whether the memorandum is required to be filed or only made available, and the address or portal for submission.
Save a dated PDF capture of each state's checklist named by state and statement year as the evidence behind the channel decision.
Flag any state whose deadline is earlier than 1 March so the package is prepared to the earliest date.
checklist.done: every state row carries a dated checklist capture, a due date, a format and a submission channel.

checklist.step: Assemble the filing package for each writing company
actions: Compile the Annual Statement blank with Exhibits 5, 6 and 7, Schedule S, the jurat page and all supplements required for the statement year.
Attach the signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion PDF received from the Appointed Actuary without re-rendering or re-signing it.
Run the NAIC validation and cross-check edits within the statutory reporting system and clear every hard edit before the package is considered ready.
Confirm the jurat page officers and the opinion signer details are consistent across the package.
Record the package version and the file hash of the opinion PDF on the filing log.
checklist.done: a validated package with the unaltered signed opinion attached exists per writing company, with the opinion file hash recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the Annual Statement and opinion through the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company filer credentials and open the Financial Data Repository annual filing area for the statement year.
Upload the annual statement data file for each writing company and resolve every validation error the repository returns before proceeding.
Upload the actuarial opinion as a PDF filing against the correct company code, statement year and filing type, and confirm the document type is set to the actuarial opinion.
Capture the submission receipt showing company code, filing type, timestamp and status and save it to the filing log.
Re-check the repository the next business day to confirm the filing status has moved to received and not to rejected.
checklist.done: each writing company shows a received status in the Financial Data Repository for both the statement and the opinion, with receipts saved.

checklist.step: Submit to the states that do not take the NAIC copy
actions: Work the matrix rows flagged as requiring a direct submission and open each department's own filing portal or email address from the saved checklist capture.
Upload or transmit the statement and opinion in the format the state names, matching file naming to the state's convention where one is specified.
Pay any annual statement filing fee through the state's stated method and record the payment reference on the matrix row.
Capture the portal acknowledgement or the delivery receipt and attach it to the matrix row the same day.
checklist.done: every direct-submission state has an acknowledgement or receipt and, where applicable, a recorded fee payment reference.

checklist.step: Despatch the hard-copy and wet-signature states
actions: For each hard-copy state, print the statement and the opinion, obtain wet signatures where required and assemble the package to the state's stated collation.
Despatch by tracked courier addressed to the department's filings unit, allowing enough transit time to arrive on or before the state's due date.
Record the courier tracking number and the expected delivery date on the matrix row.
Confirm delivery and attach the proof of delivery to the row - a despatch without confirmed delivery is not a completed filing.
checklist.done: every hard-copy state shows a tracking number and a confirmed proof of delivery dated on or before its due date.

checklist.step: Deliver the memorandum and issues summary to the Alabama domiciliary regulator
actions: Assemble the Actuarial Memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary in the format the Alabama Department of Insurance requests.
Transmit to the ALDOI financial regulation contact by the stated channel by 15 March and mark the transmission as confidential under the Standard Valuation Law confidentiality provisions.
For every other state, confirm from the saved checklist whether the memorandum must be filed or only made available on request, and record the answer on the matrix row.
Capture the ALDOI acknowledgement and file it with the filing confirmations.
checklist.done: the memorandum and issues summary are delivered to ALDOI by 15 March with an acknowledgement on file, and every other state's requirement is recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile confirmations back to the jurisdiction matrix daily during the filing window
actions: Each business day from 20 February, update the matrix status per row: not started, submitted, acknowledged, rejected.
Chase any row still at submitted after two business days with the department contact recorded on the checklist capture.
Escalate any rejection to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day with the rejection reason text pasted onto the row.
Publish the daily status count to the Chief Financial Officer until every row reads acknowledged.
checklist.done: the matrix reaches acknowledged on every row, with a dated daily status trail through the filing window.

checklist.step: Handle rejections and resubmissions inside the deadline
actions: Read the rejection reason and classify it: data validation failure, wrong document type, missing supplement, wrong company code, or format not accepted.
Correct at source - re-run the statement validation or re-request the correct PDF from the Appointed Actuary - rather than re-uploading the same file.
Resubmit and confirm the new acknowledgement, keeping both the rejection and the acceptance on the matrix row.
Where a correction cannot be made before the deadline, notify the department in writing before the due date and record the contact name and response.
checklist.done: every rejection is classified, corrected at source, resubmitted and acknowledged, or notified to the department before the due date.

checklist.step: File any amended opinion as a formal amended filing
actions: Where the opinion or the reserves change after filing, obtain a re-signed opinion from the Appointed Actuary carrying a new signature date.
Submit an amended annual statement filing in the NAIC Financial Data Repository marked as an amendment, and repeat to every direct-submission state.
Write a short cover explanation naming what changed and why, cleared by Regulatory Counsel before it is sent.
Record the amendment on the matrix as a separate row so the original and amended filings are both traceable.
checklist.done: every amendment carries a re-signed opinion, an amended filing in each channel and a counsel-cleared explanation.

checklist.step: Verify the filed document is the signed original
actions: Download the opinion PDF back from the NAIC Financial Data Repository and from two direct-submission state portals.
Compare the downloaded file hash to the hash recorded on the filing log when the signed PDF was received from the Appointed Actuary.
Open each downloaded file and confirm the signature block, signature date and Exhibit A amounts are intact and legible.
Record any mismatch as an exception and refile the correct document immediately.
checklist.done: downloaded copies hash-match the signed original and show an intact signature block and Exhibit A.

checklist.step: Track state follow-up requests arising from the filing
actions: Log every post-filing request from a department - missing supplement, opinion clarification, memorandum request - with the state, date received and stated response date.
Route content questions to the Appointed Actuary and filing-mechanics questions to the Regulatory Filing Specialist the same day.
Track each request to a sent response and record the response date and the document sent.
Report any request open more than 10 business days to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: every post-filing request is logged, routed, answered and closed with the response document recorded.

checklist.step: Escalate any jurisdiction still unfiled at the deadline
actions: Receive the 2 March exception sweep listing any jurisdiction with no acknowledgement dated on or before 1 March.
Decide and record the action per jurisdiction: immediate submission with a late explanation, or a written extension request to the department.
Instruct Regulatory Counsel to draft any communication that admits a late filing and clear it before it is sent.
Record the decision, the owner and the date on the exception log - not filing is never an option.
checklist.done: every unfiled jurisdiction has a written, owned decision and a counsel-cleared communication where lateness is admitted.

checklist.step: Close the filing cycle with a completeness certification
actions: Produce the final matrix showing every writing-company and jurisdiction pair with its confirmation reference and confirmation date.
Certify in writing to the Chief Financial Officer that every licensed jurisdiction holds a filed statement and opinion for the statement year.
List any exception carried forward with its owner and remediation date on the same certificate.
Circulate the certificate to the Appointed Actuary and the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: a signed completeness certificate lists a confirmation reference for every jurisdiction and names any carried-forward exception.

checklist.step: Archive the filing evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the filed statement package, opinion PDF, jurisdiction matrix, all acknowledgements, courier proofs and fee receipts into the compliance evidence repository.
Index by writing company, NAIC company code, jurisdiction and statement year and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the memorandum and issues summary are stored under restricted access with the confidentiality marking preserved.
Confirm the record set is retrievable by jurisdiction and statement year before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the filing evidence set is archived, indexed by jurisdiction and year, and labelled for 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of required filings from the licence register
actions: Extract the certificate of authority register at 31 December independently of the filing team and build your own writing-company by jurisdiction matrix.
Compare your matrix row count to the filing team's frozen matrix and investigate every difference before sampling.
Confirm licences surrendered during the year are still in scope where the company wrote business in the statement year.
Sign the population as complete, naming the register extract date.
testing.done: an independently built jurisdiction matrix reconciles to the filing team's matrix and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every population row to a filing confirmation
actions: Match each population row to a confirmation - Financial Data Repository receipt, portal acknowledgement or courier proof of delivery.
Check the confirmation date is on or before the jurisdiction's own due date, using the state due date and not the 1 March default.
List rows with no confirmation, with a confirmation dated after the due date, or with a confirmation for the wrong company code, as automatic exceptions.
Quantify days late for each late row.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a dated confirmation or listed as an exception with days late computed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of jurisdictions to trace end to end
actions: Take 100 percent of hard-copy states, 100 percent of direct-submission states and the Alabama domiciliary row.
Take 15 further jurisdictions at random using a recorded seed from the remaining rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every jurisdiction that produced a rejection or a prior-year exception as a mandatory row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all hard-copy, direct-submission, domiciliary and previously exceptional jurisdictions is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the channel determination against each state's checklist
actions: Open each sampled state's published annual statement filing checklist for the statement year and read the actuarial opinion requirement yourself.
Reach an independent conclusion on the required channel, format, due date and whether the memorandum must be filed, before reading the matrix row.
Compare to the recorded determination and treat a right channel with a wrong due date as an exception.
Capture the checklist page relied on into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent channel and deadline determination with the source checklist captured.

testing.step: Retrieve the filed opinion and prove it is the signed original
actions: Download the opinion PDF from the NAIC Financial Data Repository for each sampled writing company and from each sampled state portal.
Compute the file hash and compare it to the hash recorded on the filing log at the point the signed PDF was received.
Open each file and confirm the signature block, the signature date on or before 1 March and the Exhibit A amounts.
Treat any re-rendered, unsigned or truncated document as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled filed opinion hash-matches the signed original and shows an intact signature block and date.

testing.step: Trace the filed statement figures to the opinion exhibits
actions: Open the filed Annual Statement for each sampled writing company in the Financial Data Repository and read Exhibits 5, 6 and 7 as filed.
Compare each to the corresponding Exhibit A line on the filed opinion and record any difference to the dollar.
Confirm the jurat page and the opinion name the same writing company, NAIC company code and statement year.
Where an amended filing exists, confirm the amended opinion accompanies the amended statement in every channel.
testing.done: filed statement exhibits and filed opinion exhibits agree to the dollar for every sampled company, amendments included.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline arithmetic including transit time
actions: For hard-copy states, compare the courier despatch date plus the quoted transit days to the state due date and confirm the proof of delivery date meets it.
For the Alabama domiciliary memorandum, compare the transmission date to 15 March and compute days late where missed.
For any state with an earlier-than-1-March deadline, confirm the package was prepared and submitted to that earlier date.
List every row where the plan relied on a same-day delivery assumption as a control weakness even where delivery succeeded.
testing.done: every deadline is recomputed including transit, and reliance on same-day delivery is flagged as a weakness.

testing.step: Test rejection handling and post-filing request closure
actions: Pull every rejection recorded in the filing window and confirm each has a classified reason, a source correction and a subsequent acknowledgement.
Confirm no rejection was cleared by re-uploading an identical file.
Pull every post-filing department request and confirm a response document and response date are recorded.
Flag any request open more than 10 business days at the time of testing.
testing.done: every rejection traces to a source correction and an acknowledgement, and every department request has a recorded response.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the writing company, the jurisdiction, the days late and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause - matrix omission, stale state checklist, missed hard-copy transit, rejected submission not reworked, wrong document filed - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any jurisdiction filed late, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing completeness test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unfiled-jurisdiction threshold and state the number of jurisdictions filed late.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Compliance Officer, who prepared and submitted none of the filings, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any late filings to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Code Title 27, Chapter 36A); Arizona, California and Connecticut confirmed to require asset adequacy analysis on the same VM-30 basis

In-scope processes.value: Annual 12/31 asset adequacy analysis for every reserve segment - asset portfolio assignment, economic scenario generation, reinvestment and disinvestment strategy, liability cash flow projection, sensitivity testing and determination of any additional reserve

In-scope systems.value: Cash flow models and scenario engine in the actuarial modeling platform, fed by the invested asset file from the investment accounting system and the liability extract from policy administration

Compliance procedure documented.value: Asset Adequacy and Cash Flow Testing Procedure - segmentation and asset assignment, scenario set selection and calibration, reinvestment strategy documentation, projection runs, sensitivity suite, additional reserve determination and memorandum Section 3 write-up

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Appointed Actuary under VM-G governance with the Chief Investment Officer signing the asset assignment and reinvestment strategy; reviewed annually before the 12/31 run

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Asset portfolio and liability model locked by 31 January, projection and sensitivity runs complete by 10 February, additional reserve decision by 15 February so it is booked before the 1 March Annual Statement, and the testing documentation complete by the 15 March memorandum date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Year-end calendar tasks at asset file delivery, scenario set release, model lock, run completion, sensitivity review and additional reserve decision, each alerting the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary and the Appointed Actuary 5 and 2 working days ahead

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Asset adequacy testing report - segmentation and asset assignment, scenario set identifier and calibration evidence, reinvestment strategy, projection output by scenario, sensitivity results and the additional reserve calculation - retained 7 years from the valuation date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Asset overlaps or shortfalls between segments, uncalibrated scenario sets, reinvestment strategies inconsistent with the actual investment policy, missing sensitivity runs and unbooked indicated additional reserves are logged with disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Appointed Actuary signs off any deficiency in the testing that is accepted rather than corrected, and every decision not to book an indicated additional reserve

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every reserve segment subject to asset adequacy analysis for the 12/31 valuation, with its assigned asset portfolio, scenario runs and sensitivity results

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Assigned asset statement value must equal the segment reserve plus any intended surplus within 0.5 percent, and the sum of assigned assets across segments must not exceed the invested asset total; any segment showing a shortfall under the prescribed scenarios with no additional reserve booked is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual at 12/31, so the test runs once per year in February on the full segment population, with an interim review of the reinvestment strategy at Q3

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, calibrated or run the cash flow models under test, and must not report to the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual asset adequacy test workpaper - segment population, asset assignment reconciliation, scenario re-runs, sensitivity re-performance and exception log - filed in the model governance repository under the valuation date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Asset adequacy testing report with segmentation, scenario descriptions, projection results and sensitivity exhibits, cross-referenced into the Actuarial Memorandum Section 3 and producible to an ALDOI examiner within 10 business days
