checklist.step: Define the reserve segments and confirm the analysis basis for each
actions: List every reserve segment to be tested, taking the segmentation from the investment segmentation plan agreed with the Chief Investment Officer.
Record for each segment the products included, the reserve amount at the valuation date and the analysis method - full cash flow testing, gross premium reserve, demonstration or risk-theoretic.
Justify in writing any segment analysed by a method other than cash flow testing, naming the characteristic that makes cash flow testing unnecessary.
Confirm the segment list covers 100 percent of the reserves in the opinion scope with no product falling between segments.
Circulate the segment definition to the Appointed Actuary for agreement before assets are assigned.
checklist.done: every product in the opinion scope sits in exactly one segment with a named and justified analysis method.

checklist.step: Assign the invested asset portfolio to each segment as of 12/31
actions: Extract the invested asset file at 31 December with CUSIP, asset class, statement value, book value, market value, coupon, maturity, call features, NAIC designation and segment tag.
Reconcile the total statement value of the extract to Schedule D, Schedule B and Schedule BA totals and to the general ledger invested asset balance.
Confirm each asset carries exactly one segment tag and that no asset is assigned to two segments or left untagged.
Deliver the file to the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary with the reconciliation attached and the extract timestamp recorded.
checklist.done: a reconciled 12/31 asset file with unique segment tags ties to Schedules D, B and BA and to the ledger.

checklist.step: Prove the asset assignment covers the liabilities it is meant to support
actions: For each segment compare the assigned asset statement value to the segment reserve plus any intended surplus and compute the difference in dollars and percent.
Investigate any segment outside 0.5 percent with the Investment Operations Manager and either re-tag assets or document the intended surplus explicitly.
Sum the assigned assets across segments and confirm the total does not exceed the company invested asset total - overlap is a hard stop.
Record the starting asset amount used in each model run and the basis on which any surplus asset was included or excluded.
checklist.done: each segment's assigned assets match its reserve plus intended surplus within 0.5 percent and no asset is double counted.

checklist.step: Select and validate the economic scenario set
actions: Load the scenario set required for the valuation date - the prescribed deterministic interest rate scenarios for cash flow testing and the prescribed stochastic generator output where stochastic analysis applies.
Set the starting yield curve to the Treasury curve at 31 December and confirm the generator was seeded with that curve, not a stale one.
Run the calibration checks the Valuation Manual specifies and record the results against each criterion.
Record the scenario set identifier, generation date, scenario count and calibration evidence in the model governance repository.
Release the set to the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary and freeze it for the cycle.
checklist.done: a frozen, calibrated scenario set seeded on the 12/31 curve is released with its identifier and calibration evidence recorded.

checklist.step: Document the reinvestment and disinvestment strategy actually modelled
actions: Write down the modelled reinvestment strategy: target asset mix, quality distribution, maturity profile, assumed spreads over Treasury and the prescribed default cost assumptions.
Write down the disinvestment rule: which assets are sold first, at what price basis, and how negative cash flow is funded including any borrowing assumption.
Have the Chief Investment Officer confirm in writing that the modelled strategy is consistent with the board-approved investment policy and current practice.
Where the modelled strategy is deliberately more conservative than practice, state that and the reason.
File the strategy note with the testing workpapers and reference it in the memorandum.
checklist.done: a written reinvestment and disinvestment strategy exists, confirmed by the Chief Investment Officer as consistent with investment policy.

checklist.step: Build and validate the liability cash flow model
actions: Load the seriatim or model-point liability file for each segment and reconcile the model point reserve to the seriatim statutory reserve within 1 percent by segment.

Set the liability assumptions used for testing - mortality, morbidity, lapse, premium persistency, policyholder behaviour under interest sensitivity - and state where they differ from the reserve assumptions and why.
Include non-guaranteed element actions the company would actually take and document the mechanism and any limits on them.
Run a static validation projecting one period and comparing modelled premium, benefit and expense cash flows to the prior year actuals.
Record the model version and the model point compression method in the run log.
checklist.done: the liability model reconciles to statutory reserves within 1 percent by segment and passes a static one-period validation.

checklist.step: Run the projection under the prescribed scenarios
actions: Run the asset and liability projection for every segment over each prescribed interest rate scenario for the full projection horizon.
Capture per scenario the ending surplus, the accumulated deficiency and the first period in which any deficiency arises.
Confirm each run completed without truncation and that the run log names the asset file, liability file, assumption tag and scenario id.
Store the per-scenario output in the model governance repository under the valuation date and the segment name.
Flag any segment showing a deficiency in any prescribed scenario for the additional reserve decision.
checklist.done: every segment has completed runs across all prescribed scenarios with per-scenario surplus and deficiency captured.

checklist.step: Run the sensitivity suite around the key assumptions
actions: Run sensitivities on the assumptions the result is most exposed to - mortality or morbidity level, lapse level and interest sensitivity of lapse, expense inflation, default cost and reinvestment spread.
Size each sensitivity as a stated shock, for example lapse plus and minus 25 percent, mortality plus 10 percent, spreads down 50 basis points, and record the shock used.
Tabulate the change in accumulated deficiency for each sensitivity by segment and identify the two assumptions driving the result.
Present the table to the Appointed Actuary as the basis for the moderately adverse conditions judgement.
checklist.done: a sensitivity table by segment shows the quantified impact of each named shock and identifies the dominant assumptions.

checklist.step: Determine and book any additional reserve indicated
actions: For each segment showing a deficiency, compute the additional reserve as the amount that removes the accumulated deficiency on the governing scenario basis.
Decide whether aggregation across segments is permitted and, if used, document the basis and which segments were aggregated.
Agree the amount with the Chief Financial Officer and confirm the journal is posted before the Annual Statement is finalised for the 1 March filing.
Where an indicated additional reserve is not booked, record the reasoning and obtain the Chief Actuary sign-off.
Reference the additional reserve amount in the opinion and in the memorandum.
checklist.done: every indicated additional reserve is computed, decided, and either booked before filing or documented with Chief Actuary sign-off.

checklist.step: Test the results against moderately adverse conditions
actions: Define what moderately adverse means for each segment in terms of the sensitivity shocks, and state it in writing rather than leaving it implicit.
Read across the sensitivity table and confirm the reserves remain sufficient under those conditions after any additional reserve.
Where a segment fails under moderately adverse conditions, describe the block, the driver and the management action available in the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary.
Record the conclusion and the evidence relied on in the testing report.
checklist.done: moderately adverse conditions are defined per segment and the sufficiency conclusion under them is documented with evidence.

checklist.step: Reconcile the testing back to the reported reserves
actions: Tie the starting liability in each cash flow model to the statutory reserve reported for that segment in Exhibits 5 and 6.
Tie the starting assets to the segment tags in the Schedule D reconciliation and to the ledger invested asset balance.
Produce a one-page reconciliation showing total tested reserves against total opinion-scope reserves with any gap named and explained.
Refuse to sign the reconciliation where any opinion-scope reserve is untested.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows tested reserves equal opinion-scope reserves with every gap named and explained.

checklist.step: Put the testing through independent model review
actions: Review the model change log since the prior year-end for the cash flow models and require a quantified impact for each change.
Check the run logs show the frozen scenario set, the frozen assumption tag and the reconciled asset file - a run on any other input must be re-run.
Challenge the reinvestment strategy and the policyholder behaviour assumptions against the sensitivity results and record the challenge and response.
Record the review sign-off in the model governance repository against the valuation date.
checklist.done: an independent review sign-off exists naming the model versions, inputs and challenges raised and resolved.

checklist.step: Write the asset adequacy section of the Actuarial Memorandum
actions: Write the VM-30 Section 3 content: segmentation, asset assignment, scenario descriptions, reinvestment strategy, liability assumptions and their sources, model description and validation, results by scenario and the sensitivity exhibits.
Include the additional reserve determination with its arithmetic so a reviewing actuary can reproduce it.
Cross-reference every exhibit to the underlying run output stored in the model governance repository.
Deliver the section to the Appointed Actuary in time for the 15 March memorandum availability date.
checklist.done: the memorandum asset adequacy section covers every VM-30 required element and is cross-referenced to stored run output.

checklist.step: Log deficiencies in the testing itself as exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for any asset overlap or shortfall, any uncalibrated scenario set, any missing sensitivity run and any segment tested by a method with no written justification.
Assign a root cause and an owner and set a remediation date inside the next annual cycle.
Escalate to the Appointed Actuary any deficiency that could change the adequacy conclusion for the current year.
Track each issue to closure and confirm the fix is reflected in the following year's procedure.
checklist.done: every testing deficiency is an open issue with a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

checklist.step: Archive the asset adequacy testing evidence
actions: Move the testing report, asset file and its reconciliation, scenario calibration evidence, reinvestment strategy note, run logs, per-scenario output, sensitivity tables and the additional reserve calculation into the compliance evidence repository.
Index by valuation date, writing company and segment and apply the 7-year retention label.
Preserve the confidentiality marking that applies to the memorandum-supporting material and restrict access accordingly.
Confirm the evidence is retrievable by valuation date and segment before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the full asset adequacy evidence set is archived, indexed by segment and valuation date and labelled for 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of segments subject to asset adequacy analysis
actions: List every reserve segment from the segmentation plan and every reserve line in the opinion scope worksheet.
Match the two lists and identify any opinion-scope reserve with no segment and any segment with no reserve.
Reconcile total segment reserves to Exhibits 5, 6 and 7 in the filed Annual Statement and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete, naming the segmentation plan version and statement used.
testing.done: the segment population reconciles to the filed exhibits with no untested opinion-scope reserve, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile assigned assets to the investment source of record
actions: Re-extract the 12/31 invested asset file with segment tags independently and total statement value by segment.
Compare the totals to the asset amounts used as starting assets in each model run and record differences in dollars and percent.
Confirm the sum across segments does not exceed the Schedule D, B and BA totals and the ledger invested asset balance.
List any asset tagged to two segments or untagged as an automatic exception.
testing.done: assigned assets reconcile by segment to the investment source and no asset is double tagged or untagged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of segments and scenarios
actions: Take 100 percent of segments holding more than 10 percent of tested reserves and 100 percent of segments showing any deficiency.
Take 5 further segments at random with a recorded seed, and within each sampled segment take the 3 worst-outcome scenarios plus 2 at random.
Record the seed, population size, stratification boundaries and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every segment with a prior-year exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all large and deficient segments plus prior exceptions is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the scenario calibration and confirm the starting curve
actions: Open the frozen scenario set and read the starting yield curve, generation date and scenario count from its header.
Compare the starting curve point by point to the published Treasury curve at 31 December and flag any tenor that differs.
Re-run the prescribed calibration checks on the set and compare your results to the recorded calibration evidence.
Confirm every sampled production run log names this scenario set identifier and no other.
testing.done: the scenario set is seeded on the correct 12/31 curve, passes recalibration, and is the set named in every sampled run log.

testing.step: Re-run a sampled segment projection independently
actions: Rebuild the run for one large sampled segment from the archived asset file, liability file, assumption tag and scenario set without copying the production run settings.
Compare your ending surplus and accumulated deficiency per sampled scenario to the production output and compute the difference.
Investigate any difference over 1 percent of the segment reserve and trace it to an input, a setting or a model version difference.
Capture both run logs side by side into the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent re-run reproduces the production result within 1 percent or the difference is traced to a named cause.

testing.step: Test the reinvestment strategy against actual investment practice
actions: Read the modelled reinvestment strategy note and extract the target mix, quality distribution, maturity profile and assumed spreads.
Compare each to the board-approved investment policy limits and to the actual purchases made in the year from the investment activity report.
Flag any modelled spread or quality assumption more favourable than actual practice as an exception, since it flatters the result.
Confirm the Chief Investment Officer confirmation is on file, signed and dated before the projection runs.
testing.done: the modelled strategy is no more favourable than policy and practice, with a dated Chief Investment Officer confirmation on file.

testing.step: Recompute the additional reserve arithmetic
actions: For each sampled deficient segment recompute the additional reserve as the amount that removes the accumulated deficiency on the stated governing basis.
Where aggregation across segments was used, recompute the aggregate position and confirm the aggregation basis is documented and permitted.
Trace the resulting amount to the general ledger journal and to Exhibits 5 or 6 in the filed statement.
Treat any indicated additional reserve not booked and not signed off by the Chief Actuary as a fail.
testing.done: the additional reserve is recomputed, traced to the ledger and the filed exhibits, and any unbooked amount carries a sign-off.

testing.step: Re-perform the sensitivity suite on the dominant assumptions
actions: Re-run the two sensitivities the testing named as dominant for one large sampled segment using the stated shock sizes.
Compare the change in accumulated deficiency to the recorded sensitivity table and record any difference.
Add one sensitivity the testing did not run - a combined lapse and spread shock - and report whether the conclusion survives it.
Capture the sensitivity output into the workpaper with the shock definitions.
testing.done: sampled sensitivities are reproduced, and a combined shock is run and reported against the stated conclusion.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the segment, the element affected and the effect on the adequacy conclusion.
Assign a root cause - asset tagging error, stale scenario set, unvalidated model change, optimistic reinvestment assumption, missing sensitivity - and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next annual cycle and escalate immediately anything that could change the current-year conclusion.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the asset adequacy test
actions: Compute the exception rate by segment count and by tested reserve dollars against the stated thresholds.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the Model Risk Manager, who neither built nor ran the sampled models, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any unbooked indicated reserve to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - VM-31 data section and VM-G governance expectations on valuation data quality, together with the Annual Statement Instructions requirement that Exhibits 5 and 6 tie to the underlying in-force records, under Alabama's Standard Valuation Law (Ala. Code Title 27, Chapter 36A); Arizona, California and Connecticut adopt the same Valuation Manual data requirements

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly reconciliation of the valuation in-force file to the policy administration system of record and onward to the general ledger, covering policy counts, face amount, account value, annualized premium, ceded cessions and the resulting reserve by Annual Statement line

In-scope systems.value: Valuation staging tables in the enterprise data warehouse compared against the policy administration system of record, the reinsurance administration system and the general ledger reserve accounts

Compliance procedure documented.value: Valuation Data Reconciliation Procedure - control total definitions, extract-to-source comparison, tolerance thresholds by measure, exception categorisation and ageing, source-system defect routing and quarterly sign-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Chief Actuary and the Chief Data Officer, refreshed annually and whenever a policy administration release changes an in-force field used in valuation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Reconciliation complete and signed by working day 6 of each quarter close - before the reserve lock that feeds the 5/15, 8/15 and 11/15 quarterly statements - and by working day 10 of January for the 12/31 valuation feeding the 1 March Annual Statement

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarter-close calendar tasks at extract-ready, reconciliation-drafted and sign-off-due, with alerts to the Valuation Actuary, Data Quality Manager and Statutory Reporting Manager 3 and 1 working days before the sign-off date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Reconciliation report per quarter - control totals by measure and plan code, variance calculations, exception list with ageing, source defect tickets and the signed sign-off page - retained 7 years from the valuation date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Out-of-tolerance variances, unmatched policies in either direction, unmatched cessions, records defaulted rather than corrected, and any reconciliation signed with open items are logged with the reserve dollar impact and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Data Quality Manager signs off every source-system defect fix and every decision to default a record rather than correct it at source

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every plan code and Annual Statement line appearing in the quarter's valuation extract and in the policy administration in-force report, plus every ceded cession in the reinsurance administration system for the same date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Policy count and face amount within 0.1 percent, account value and annualized premium within 0.25 percent, reserve dollars within 0.5 percent by plan code; any unmatched policy carrying reserve above 25,000 dollars is a fail regardless of the percentage variance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly, so the test runs each quarter on that quarter's reconciliation with an expanded 12/31 pass covering all plan codes and the ceded cession match

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly valuation data reconciliation test workpaper - independent control totals, variance re-performance, unmatched item trace and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under the valuation date

checklist.step: Fix the reconciliation design and the control totals to be compared
actions: List the measures to be reconciled: policy count, sum insured or face amount, account value, annualized premium, paid-to-date currency, ceded face amount and reserve dollars.
Define the grain at which each measure is compared - plan code within writing company within Annual Statement line - and record it in the procedure.
Set the tolerance per measure and record it on the reconciliation template rather than deciding it after the numbers are seen.
Agree with the Data Quality Manager which system is the source of record for each measure so a difference has a direction.
Publish the template to the Actuarial Analyst before the quarter close begins.
checklist.done: a published template names every measure, its grain, its tolerance and its source of record before the close starts.

checklist.step: Produce the policy administration in-force control report
actions: Run the standard in-force report as of the quarter-end date after the month-end cycle completes, with status filters set to in force, paid up, waiver and extended term.
Produce counts and sums by plan code and writing company for each measure named on the reconciliation template.
Record the report run timestamp, the system release number and the status filter used on the report header.
Deliver the report to the Actuarial Analyst without manual adjustment - adjustments belong on the reconciliation, not in the source report.
checklist.done: an unadjusted in-force control report by plan code exists with its run timestamp, release number and status filters stated.

checklist.step: Produce the valuation extract control totals on the same basis
actions: Total the locked valuation staging table by plan code and writing company for each measure on the template.
Apply exactly the same status filter and as-of date as the in-force control report, and state both on the output.
Confirm the staging table run id matches the extract that will actually feed the valuation models this quarter.
Load both sets of totals into the reconciliation workbook side by side.
checklist.done: extract control totals are produced on the same as-of date, status filter and grain as the in-force report and loaded for comparison.

checklist.step: Compute the variance by measure and plan code and apply the tolerances
actions: Compute absolute and percentage variance per measure per plan code and flag every row outside its stated tolerance.
Rank the flagged rows by reserve dollar impact so the largest are worked first, not the largest percentages.
Summarise total variance by Annual Statement line so the effect on Exhibits 5 and 6 is visible.
Send the flagged list to the Valuation Actuary and the Data Quality Manager the same day it is produced.
checklist.done: every plan code shows a computed variance against its tolerance, with breaches ranked by reserve dollar impact.

checklist.step: Identify unmatched policies in both directions
actions: Full-outer-join the valuation extract to the policy administration in-force file on policy number and writing company.
List policies present in policy administration but absent from the extract - these are missing reserves - with their face amount and plan code.
List policies present in the extract but absent from policy administration - these are phantom reserves - with the reserve carried.
Estimate the reserve impact of each unmatched list and attach it to the reconciliation.
Flag any single unmatched policy carrying more than 25,000 dollars of reserve for same-day investigation.
checklist.done: both unmatched lists are produced with reserve impact quantified and large individual items flagged for same-day work.

checklist.step: Categorise each variance to a cause rather than a bucket
actions: Assign each flagged row a cause: timing of the extract against a late transaction batch, status mapping difference, in-year conversion or plan code change, data defect at source, or extract logic defect.
Prove timing causes by re-running the comparison with the following day's transaction file rather than asserting timing.
Separate causes that will self-correct next quarter from causes that will persist, and label them accordingly.
Record the cause and the evidence on each row of the reconciliation.
checklist.done: every flagged row carries a proven cause with evidence and a self-correcting or persistent label.

checklist.step: Route source-system defects for correction at source
actions: Raise a defect ticket per persistent source-data cause naming the field, the affected policy population, the reserve impact and the plan code.
Assign the ticket to the Policy Admin Ops Lead with a target fix release and require the fix to correct history, not just future records.
Where a record must be defaulted in valuation for this quarter, record the default value, the justification and the number of records affected for the VM-31 data section.
Sign off each default personally rather than allowing the valuation team to default records unilaterally.
checklist.done: each persistent defect has a ticket with an owner and target release, and every default is signed off with a recorded justification.

checklist.step: Reconcile the ceded cessions to the reinsurance system
actions: Extract the cession detail at the valuation date and match it to the valuation extract on policy number and treaty code.
Compare ceded face amount and ceded reserve by treaty and flag differences outside the reserve tolerance.
List policies flagged as ceded in policy administration with no cession record, and cessions with no matching in-force policy.
Tie the reconciled ceded totals to Schedule S Part 3 and attach the tie-out to the reconciliation.
checklist.done: ceded cessions match the valuation extract by treaty and tie to Schedule S Part 3, with unmatched items listed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the resulting reserves to the general ledger
actions: Pull the reserve account balances by writing company from the trial balance at the quarter end.
Compare them to the valuation aggregation by Annual Statement line and identify every difference.
Trace each difference to a posted journal, a manual top-side entry or an unposted valuation result, and clear it before sign-off.
Attach the ledger tie-out to the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: valuation reserves tie to the trial balance by writing company with every difference traced to a named entry.

checklist.step: Age the open exceptions and enforce the ageing limits
actions: Carry forward every unresolved item from prior quarters and record the quarters open against each.
Escalate any item open more than two quarters to the Chief Data Officer and the Chief Actuary with its reserve impact.
Confirm items marked self-correcting actually cleared in the following quarter, and reclassify those that did not as persistent defects.
Publish the ageing summary with the reconciliation.
checklist.done: an ageing summary shows quarters open per item and every item over two quarters is escalated with its reserve impact.

checklist.step: Write the VM-31 data section narrative from the reconciliation
actions: Summarise record counts in scope, records failing each quality rule, records corrected at source and records defaulted, with the default justification.
State the reconciliation result by measure against the tolerances and the residual unexplained variance in reserve dollars.
Describe the effect of the residual variance on the reserve and why it does not change the adequacy conclusion, or escalate if it does.
Hand the narrative to the Appointed Actuary for inclusion in the VM-31 report and the memorandum.
checklist.done: a data section narrative states counts, failures, corrections, defaults and the residual reserve variance with its effect.

checklist.step: Obtain the quarterly reconciliation sign-off before reserve lock
actions: Present the reconciliation, exception list, ageing summary and ledger tie-out to the Chief Actuary and the Data Quality Manager.
Obtain a dated signature from each confirming the reconciliation is within tolerance or that named breaches are accepted with reasons.
Refuse to release the reserve figure where any measure is outside tolerance with no accepted reason recorded.
Record the sign-off date and compare it to the working day 6 target, logging any slippage.
checklist.done: a dated dual sign-off exists before reserve lock, with any accepted breach reasoned and any slippage logged.

checklist.step: Feed the findings into the next quarter's extract and rules
actions: Add a data quality rule for every new failure mode found this quarter so it is caught at the gate rather than at reconciliation.
Fix any extract logic defect found and re-run the prior quarter comparison to confirm the fix reproduces the corrected result.
Update the pipeline to stamp the source system release number so a release change is visible in the next comparison.
Record the pipeline change and its validation in the change log.
checklist.done: each new failure mode has a gate rule, every extract defect is fixed and re-validated against the prior quarter.

checklist.step: Report the reconciliation outcome to actuarial governance
actions: Present to the actuarial governance forum the quarter's residual variance by Annual Statement line and the open exception ageing.
Highlight any item that has been open more than two quarters and name the accountable owner in the meeting.
Record the forum's direction on any item where the fix is being deferred.
Minute the outcome and file it with the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: the governance forum minutes record the residual variance, the aged items and the direction on any deferred fix.

checklist.step: Archive the reconciliation evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the reconciliation workbook, in-force control report, extract control totals, unmatched lists, defect tickets, ceded tie-out, ledger tie-out and signed sign-off page into the compliance evidence repository.
Index by valuation date, writing company and Annual Statement line and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record set is retrievable by quarter and plan code before closing the cycle.
Link the record set to the valuation workpaper pack for the same valuation date.
checklist.done: the reconciliation evidence set is archived, linked to the valuation workpapers and labelled for 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of plan codes and measures reconciled for the quarter
actions: Extract the distinct plan code and writing company combinations from the valuation staging table for the quarter-end date.
Extract the same from the policy administration in-force report and union the two lists so a plan code missing from either side is still in the population.
Reconcile the population count to the reconciliation workbook row count and investigate any plan code omitted from the reconciliation.
Sign the population as complete, naming the extract date and the report versions used.
testing.done: the plan code population is built from both sides, reconciles to the reconciliation workbook and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Re-derive the control totals independently from the source of record
actions: Run your own in-force query in the policy administration system for the quarter-end date using the documented status filters.
Total policy count, face amount, account value and annualized premium by plan code without reference to the team's report.
Compare your totals to both the in-force control report and the valuation extract totals and record any three-way difference.
Treat a difference between your query and the team's control report as a control failure in the reconciliation itself.
testing.done: independently derived control totals agree with both the in-force report and the extract, or the difference is recorded as a control failure.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of variances and unmatched items
actions: Take 100 percent of plan codes with a variance outside tolerance and 100 percent of unmatched policies carrying more than 25,000 dollars of reserve.
Take 25 policies at random with a recorded seed from the matched population to test the match itself, not only the breaks.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every item open from a prior quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all tolerance breaches, large unmatched items, matched policies and aged items is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the variance calculation and tolerance application
actions: Recompute absolute and percentage variance for each sampled plan code from the two source totals rather than from the workbook formulas.
Compare the tolerance applied to the tolerance published on the template and flag any row where the tolerance was widened after the numbers were seen.
Recompute the total variance by Annual Statement line and compare to the reconciliation summary.
Treat a row passed on a tolerance not published in advance as a fail.
testing.done: sampled variances are recomputed from source totals and every applied tolerance matches the pre-published template.

testing.step: Trace sampled policies from the valuation extract to the policy record
actions: Open the policy record for each of the 25 sampled matched policies and read issue date, issue age, sex, smoker class, face amount, mode, paid-to date and status.
Compare each field to the valuation extract row and record any mismatch at field level.
Assess whether each mismatch would change the reserve and quantify it where it would.
Capture the policy screen and the extract row into the workpaper for any mismatch.
testing.done: each sampled policy is traced field by field to the policy record with reserve-relevant mismatches quantified.

testing.step: Test the proof behind each claimed timing difference
actions: Pull every variance row categorised as a timing difference and ask for the following-day re-run evidence that proved it.
Where no re-run evidence exists, reclassify the row as unexplained and add its reserve impact to the residual variance.
Check that rows labelled self-correcting in the prior quarter actually cleared, and reclassify those that did not.
Report the reclassified residual variance against the tolerance.
testing.done: every timing claim is supported by re-run evidence or reclassified as unexplained, with the residual variance restated.

testing.step: Test the ceded cession match and the Schedule S tie
actions: Select the ten largest treaties and re-run the cession match against the valuation extract on policy number and treaty code.
Compare ceded face amount and ceded reserve by treaty to the reconciliation and record differences.
Open every policy flagged as ceded in policy administration with no cession record and determine whether reserve credit was taken anyway.
Trace the reconciled ceded total to Schedule S Part 3 in the filed statement.
testing.done: sampled treaties reconcile, no reserve credit is taken without a cession record, and the ceded total ties to Schedule S Part 3.

testing.step: Recompute the ledger tie and confirm sign-off preceded reserve lock
actions: Pull the reserve account balances by writing company from the trial balance and compare them to the valuation aggregation independently.
Trace every manual top-side entry affecting reserves to a supporting calculation and an approver.
Compare the reconciliation sign-off timestamp to the reserve lock timestamp and to the working day 6 target.
Treat a sign-off dated after the reserve lock as a control failure regardless of the numbers agreeing.
testing.done: the ledger tie is independently reproduced and the sign-off is proven to pre-date the reserve lock.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan code, the measure, the reserve dollar impact and whether the reserve was over or understated.
Assign a root cause - source data defect, extract logic defect, status mapping, unproven timing claim, tolerance widened after the fact - and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter close and require a gate rule for any new failure mode.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a gate rule where a new failure mode was found.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the reconciliation test
actions: Compute the exception rate by plan code count and by reserve dollars against the stated tolerances.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared no reconciliation in the period, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and the residual unexplained variance to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the substance of every answer given to a regulator on reserves or the opinion; the Regulatory Affairs Manager owns intake, tracking and despatch

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Alabama's Standard Valuation Law examination and information provisions (Ala. Code Title 27, Chapter 36A) with the confidentiality protection for the actuarial memorandum, read with the NAIC Financial Condition Examiners Handbook information request process; Arizona, California and Connecticut Standard Valuation Laws confirmed to carry equivalent request and confidentiality provisions

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven handling of valuation inquiries from any of the 51 jurisdictions - ALDOI domiciliary questions, lead state financial examination information requests, analyst follow-ups on the annual statement, and Valuation Analysis Working Group referrals - from intake through counsel clearance to despatch and closure

In-scope systems.value: Inquiry log and response tracking in the regulatory filing and issue tracker, with response packages assembled from the model governance repository and the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure - single intake point, same-day logging, triage and owner assignment, response drafting, confidentiality marking, counsel clearance, despatch and commitment tracking

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel concurrence on the privilege and confidentiality handling, reviewed annually and after any financial examination closes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Each inquiry tracked to the date the regulator states; default internal targets are acknowledgement within 2 business days, substantive response within 10 business days, and same-day acknowledgement for examination information requests issued during fieldwork

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker alerts at logging, at half the response window elapsed, at 2 business days before the stated due date, and daily once overdue, addressed to the assigned owner, the Appointed Actuary and the Regulatory Affairs Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Correspondence file per inquiry - the original request, the inquiry log entry, drafts, supporting exhibits sent, counsel clearance, the despatched response and the regulator acknowledgement - retained 7 years from closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Inquiries not logged on receipt, responses sent without counsel clearance where required, missed regulator due dates, confidential material sent unmarked, and commitments made to a regulator with no owner are logged with disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every late response, every correction to a response already sent, and every commitment made to a regulator before it is confirmed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every valuation-related regulator communication received in the period across all 51 jurisdictions - examination information requests, analyst questions, opinion and memorandum follow-ups and Valuation Analysis Working Group referrals

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any inquiry answered after the regulator's stated due date without a documented agreed extension is a fail; any response sent without required counsel clearance is a fail; any confidential memorandum material sent without the confidentiality marking is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven, so the test runs quarterly over that quarter's inquiry population, with 100 percent coverage of any financial examination information requests

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, cleared or despatched any response in the population under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulator inquiry response test workpaper - inquiry population, mailbox reconciliation, timeliness recomputation, clearance evidence and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Inquiry log export with request date, stated due date, response date and outcome, plus the full correspondence file for any inquiry, producible to an ALDOI examiner within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Appointed Actuary is the named contact for reserve and opinion questions and signs the substantive answer; the Regulatory Affairs Manager despatches and Regulatory Counsel clears anything touching an error, a restatement or privileged material

checklist.step: Publish a single intake point for valuation inquiries and name the contacts
actions: Establish one monitored mailbox for regulator correspondence and register it with the Alabama Department of Insurance and each state's financial analysis contact.
Name the Appointed Actuary as the valuation contact and the Regulatory Affairs Manager as the coordination contact in the annual statement contact record.
Instruct the Appointed Actuary, Chief Actuary and Statutory Reporting Manager to forward any direct regulator contact into the mailbox the same day it arrives.
Publish the intake rule to the actuarial and reporting teams and repeat it at the start of each examination.
checklist.done: one registered intake mailbox exists with named valuation and coordination contacts, and direct contacts are forwarded same day.

checklist.step: Log every inquiry on the day it arrives
actions: Create a tracker entry per inquiry capturing the regulator, jurisdiction, examiner or analyst name, date received, channel, the request text verbatim and the stated due date.
Attach the original request document or email as received, unedited.
Assign a unique inquiry reference and use it on every document in the response package.
Where no due date is stated, set the internal default of 10 business days and record that it is an internal date, not a regulator date.
checklist.done: every inquiry has a same-day tracker entry with the verbatim request, the original attachment and a due date marked regulator-stated or internal.

checklist.step: Triage the inquiry and assign the substantive owner
actions: Classify the inquiry: reserve methodology, assumption or margin, asset adequacy, data quality, opinion or memorandum content, filing mechanics, or examination information request.

Assign the owner - Appointed Actuary for methodology and opinion, ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary for asset adequacy, Valuation Actuary for data and computation, Regulatory Reporting Manager for filing mechanics.
Decide whether Regulatory Counsel clearance is required and record the reason where it is - anything touching an error, a restatement, a qualification or privileged material always is.
Set the internal drafting deadline at least 3 business days before the regulator due date so clearance has room.
checklist.done: every inquiry has a classification, a named substantive owner, a clearance decision and an internal drafting deadline.

checklist.step: Acknowledge receipt to the regulator
actions: Send an acknowledgement within 2 business days naming the inquiry reference, the assigned contact and the date by which the response will be provided.
Where the stated due date is not achievable, request an extension in the same acknowledgement with a specific alternative date and a reason.
Record the acknowledgement and any extension granted, with the granting examiner's name, on the tracker entry.
Never let a request pass its due date without either a response or an agreed and recorded extension.
checklist.done: every inquiry is acknowledged within 2 business days with a response date, and any extension is recorded with the granting examiner named.

checklist.step: Interpret the question precisely before drafting
actions: Read the request against the filed opinion, memorandum and statement exhibits it refers to and identify exactly which figure or statement is being questioned.
Where the request is ambiguous, ask the examiner a clarifying question in writing rather than answering a question that was not asked.
Identify whether the answer will require running a model, producing an exhibit, or only explaining an existing document, and tell the owner which.
Record the interpretation on the tracker so the response can be checked against the question later.
checklist.done: the recorded interpretation names the specific figure or statement questioned and the work required to answer it.

checklist.step: Assemble the supporting evidence from the archived workpapers
actions: Pull the archived workpapers for the valuation date in question - scope register, assumption memo, exclusion tests, run logs, aggregation worksheet, reconciliation and asset adequacy output.
Extract only the exhibits that answer the question and record the source reference for each so the examiner can navigate back.
Re-run any figure the examiner asks for on the archived model version and inputs, never on the current version, and state the version used.
Flag any difference between the archived result and the re-run immediately to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the evidence pack contains only responsive exhibits, each with a source reference and the archived model version stated.

checklist.step: Draft the response answering the question asked
actions: Draft a response that restates the question, gives the direct answer first, then the supporting explanation and the exhibit references.
Cite the Valuation Manual section and the Alabama Standard Valuation Law provision relied on where the answer rests on a methodology choice.
Do not volunteer material beyond the scope of the question, and do not omit a fact that makes the answer misleading.
Where the answer reveals an error, state the error, its reserve impact and the remediation plan in the same response.
Attach the exhibit index listing every document enclosed with its page count.
checklist.done: the draft answers the question directly, cites its authority, discloses any error with impact, and carries a complete exhibit index.

checklist.step: Apply the confidentiality marking before anything leaves
actions: Identify any enclosure drawn from the Actuarial Memorandum, the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary or the VM-31 report.
Mark those documents confidential under the Standard Valuation Law confidentiality provisions and state the marking in the cover letter.
Confirm the transmission channel is the one the regulator specified for confidential material and use no other.
Record on the tracker which enclosures were confidentiality-marked and by what channel they were sent.
checklist.done: every memorandum-derived enclosure is confidentiality-marked and sent on the regulator's specified channel, with both recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance where required
actions: Read the draft against the request and confirm it answers the question without creating an unintended admission.
Clear or amend any statement of error, restatement, qualification or remediation commitment, and confirm the reserve impact figure quoted is the one the Appointed Actuary will stand behind.
Confirm no privileged material is enclosed inadvertently and that confidentiality markings are correct.
Record the clearance with your name and date on the tracker entry - a response in a clearance-required category cannot be despatched without it.
checklist.done: a dated counsel clearance is recorded for every response in a clearance-required category.

checklist.step: Despatch the response and capture the regulator acknowledgement
actions: Send the response to the named examiner or analyst by the specified channel, quoting the inquiry reference in the subject.
Where the regulator uses an examination portal, upload to the request item so the response is linked to the request the examiner raised.
Capture the delivery confirmation or portal receipt and attach it to the tracker entry with the despatch timestamp.
Chase for acknowledgement if none is received within 5 business days and record the chase.
checklist.done: the response is despatched on the specified channel with a captured receipt and the despatch timestamp on the tracker.

checklist.step: Track every commitment made to the regulator to an owner and a date
actions: Extract every forward-looking statement in the despatched response - a remediation, a change to next year's method, an additional analysis to be supplied.
Raise a commitment record for each with an owner, a delivery date and the exact wording promised to the regulator.
Report open commitments monthly to the Head of Compliance and the Appointed Actuary until closed.
Confirm delivery to the regulator when the commitment is met and record the confirmation.
checklist.done: every commitment made in a response has a record, an owner, a date and a delivery confirmation on closure.

checklist.step: Handle examination information requests on examination timelines
actions: During a financial examination, acknowledge each information request the same day and route it to the substantive owner within 4 hours.
Maintain a request status board visible to the examination team showing each request, its owner, its due date and its status.
Hold a daily stand-up with the Appointed Actuary and Statutory Reporting Manager during fieldwork to clear blockers on open requests.
Escalate any request at risk of missing the examiner's date to the Chief Financial Officer before the date, not after.
checklist.done: every examination request is acknowledged same day, tracked on a visible board, and at-risk items are escalated before the due date.

checklist.step: Close the inquiry and record the outcome
actions: Close the tracker entry only when the regulator confirms the matter is resolved or the examination workpaper is signed off.
Record the outcome: accepted, further information requested, finding raised, or referred onward.
Where a finding was raised, link the tracker entry to the remediation issue and its owner.
Compute and record the elapsed days from receipt to despatch and from despatch to closure.
checklist.done: every closed inquiry records an outcome, any linked finding, and the elapsed days from receipt to despatch and to closure.

checklist.step: Review inquiry themes for underlying control weaknesses
actions: Each quarter group the closed inquiries by theme - assumption support, data quality, disclosure clarity, filing mechanics - and count them.
Where a theme recurs across jurisdictions, raise a control improvement action against the underlying process rather than treating each inquiry separately.
Present the themes and actions to the actuarial governance forum with the Appointed Actuary.
Feed recurring disclosure themes into next year's memorandum drafting so the question is pre-answered.
checklist.done: quarterly themes are counted, recurring themes have a control action, and disclosure themes feed the next memorandum.

checklist.step: Archive the correspondence file for the retention period
actions: Move the complete correspondence file - request, log entry, interpretation note, evidence pack, drafts, counsel clearance, despatched response, receipts and acknowledgements - into the compliance evidence repository.
Index by inquiry reference, jurisdiction, regulator and valuation date and apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label.
Preserve restricted access on any confidentiality-marked enclosure.
Confirm the file is retrievable by jurisdiction and inquiry reference before closing.
checklist.done: the complete correspondence file is archived, access-restricted where confidential and labelled for 7-year retention from closure.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation inquiries received in the quarter
actions: Export every tracker entry classified as a valuation inquiry with a receipt date inside the quarter, across all 51 jurisdictions.
Add every examination information request from the examination request board for any examination open in the quarter.
Reconcile the tracker count to the intake mailbox message count for regulator senders so an unlogged inquiry cannot hide.
Sign the population as complete, naming the export date and the mailbox search terms used.
testing.done: the inquiry population reconciles to the intake mailbox and the examination board and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the mailbox and the Appointed Actuary's direct correspondence to the log
actions: Search the intake mailbox for messages from state department domains in the quarter and match each to a tracker entry.
Ask the Appointed Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager for any direct regulator contact received outside the mailbox and match those too.
List every regulator message with no tracker entry as an automatic exception, whatever its apparent significance.
Compare the tracker logging date to the message receipt date and flag any logged later than the same day.
testing.done: every regulator message traces to a same-day tracker entry or is listed as an unlogged-inquiry exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of inquiries to re-perform
actions: Take 100 percent of examination information requests, 100 percent of inquiries in a clearance-required category and 100 percent of inquiries answered late.
Take 15 further inquiries at random with a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every inquiry with an open commitment from a prior quarter as a mandatory row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all examination, clearance-required, late and open-commitment inquiries is documented.

testing.step: Recompute the timeliness of acknowledgement and response
actions: For each sampled inquiry recompute business days from receipt to acknowledgement against the 2 business day target.
Recompute business days from receipt to despatch against the regulator's stated due date, or the internal 10 business day default where none was stated.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm the tracker records the granting examiner's name and the agreed date, and recompute against that date.
Treat an unevidenced extension as no extension and count the response as late.
testing.done: acknowledgement and response timeliness are recomputed for every sampled inquiry, with unevidenced extensions treated as late.

testing.step: Re-read the request and judge whether the response answered it
actions: Read the verbatim request text for each sampled inquiry and form your own view of what was asked before reading the response.
Read the despatched response and mark each element of the request as answered, partly answered or unanswered.
Check the cited Valuation Manual section and Alabama Standard Valuation Law provision are the ones that actually govern the point.
Flag any response that is accurate but non-responsive as an exception, since it invites a follow-up request.
testing.done: each sampled response is marked element by element against the request, with non-responsive answers flagged.

testing.step: Verify counsel clearance and confidentiality handling
actions: For each sampled inquiry in a clearance-required category, confirm a dated clearance record exists and pre-dates the despatch timestamp.
Open the despatched package and confirm every memorandum-derived enclosure carries the confidentiality marking and the cover letter states it.
Confirm the transmission channel used matches the channel the regulator specified for confidential material.
Treat a clearance dated after despatch, or an unmarked confidential enclosure, as a fail.
testing.done: every clearance-required response has a clearance pre-dating despatch and every confidential enclosure is marked and correctly channelled.

testing.step: Trace response exhibits back to the archived valuation workpapers
actions: Take five exhibits from sampled responses and locate the source workpaper in the model governance repository by the stated source reference.
Confirm the figure sent matches the archived workpaper to the dollar and that the archived model version named is the version in the repository.
Where a figure was re-run for the response, confirm the run log names the archived model version and inputs, not the current ones.
Record any figure sent to a regulator that cannot be traced to an archived workpaper as a serious exception.
testing.done: every sampled exhibit traces to an archived workpaper at the stated version and matches to the dollar.

testing.step: Test commitment tracking and delivery
actions: Read each sampled despatched response and extract every forward-looking commitment made to the regulator.
Match each to a commitment record with an owner, a delivery date and the promised wording, and list any commitment with no record.
For commitments past their delivery date, confirm delivery to the regulator was made and confirmed.
Report any commitment made to a regulator and not delivered directly to the Head of Compliance.
testing.done: every commitment in a sampled response has a tracked record and past-due commitments are proven delivered or escalated.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the jurisdiction, the inquiry reference, the days late where applicable and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause - inquiry not logged, intake bypassed, clearance skipped, confidentiality marking missed, exhibit untraceable, commitment untracked - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any late response to a financial examination request, notify the Chief Financial Officer the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the inquiry response test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for late responses, missing clearance and unmarked confidential material.
State the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Compliance Manager, who drafted, cleared and despatched none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any missed regulator deadline to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.
